title: fix(driver-sql): a refused SQLite connect() closes the connection it opened
body:
Fixes #25084

Clause-②: no (resource release only: no response, status, error, outcome or export moves)
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changed

`SqlDriver.connect()` (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts`) now closes what a refused SQLite connect opened before it rejects. On any rejection of a SQLite `connect()`, the new `releaseRefusedSqliteConnection()` destroys the Knex pool and puts a fresh, empty one in its place (`knex.destroy()` then `knex.initialize()`). Then the ORIGINAL error is rethrown unchanged: the same object, so the same class, code, message and `cause`. A release that itself fails is logged at `warn`, and the original error is still the one thrown.

This is the driver seam the claim takes. Every caller benefits: the connection service's degraded path (which never disconnects a rejected handle), the development resolver, the admin test-connection probe, and a direct driver user. The caller seam in `service-datasource` is not touched.

## Measured before the edit (at `origin/main` `03966ceae`)

**Every rejection path of `connect()`, and what is open at that point:**

| path | rejects with | pool / handle open when it rejects? |
|---|---|---|
| `ensureDatabaseExists`, SQLite: `makeDatabaseDirectory` fails | `SqliteDatabaseFileError` (directory could not be made; a dangling link) | No. It runs before any statement, so the pool has never opened a connection. |
| `ensureDatabaseExists`, pg / mysql: `SELECT 1` fails with any code but database-missing | the driver error | No. The connection itself could not be made, so the pool holds none. |
| `ensureDatabaseExists`, pg / mysql: `createDatabase()` fails | the driver error | No. Its admin Knex is destroyed in its own `finally`, and the main pool holds no connection (its `SELECT 1` failed). |
| `applyAutoVacuumIncremental`: first statement answers `SQLITE_NOTADB` / `SQLITE_CORRUPT` | `SqliteDatabaseFileError` | **Yes.** better-sqlite3 opened the file to answer, and the pool keeps that connection. For a header that says WAL, `-shm` and an empty `-wal` sit beside the file. |
| `applyAutoVacuumIncremental`: `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` | `SqliteDatabaseFileError` | No. The open itself failed, so no connection was created. |
| `applySqliteJournalMode` / `verifyWalReadable` | never rejects: every failure is caught and logged | — |

So the only rejection that holds a handle is a SQLite file refusal after the open. The release is scoped to SQLite (`if (this.isSqlite)`): no server-dialect rejection holds a connection, and destroying a server pool on a re-connect of a live, host-adopted driver would abort queries in flight for nothing.

**Reuse after a rejection:** yes, it happens. The connection service's `connect()` and `reconnect()` build a new handle per attempt through `factory.create`. But `createPrebuiltDriverFactory` returns the SAME instance on every `create()`, so a host-adopted driver is connected again on the same object. The admin probe (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts`) builds a driver per test and `disconnect()`s it in `finally`, so it never leaked a handle. That answers the card's NOT MEASURED item. The development resolver closes its probe (`closeQuietly`). So the release must leave the instance reusable. Destroying alone would not: Knex then answers every statement with a code-less "Unable to acquire a connection", so a second `connect()` would log it as an auto_vacuum failure and RESOLVE over a datasource that cannot run one query. Ablation B below measures exactly that. Hence the fresh pool.

**`disconnect()` today:** `await this.knex.destroy()`. Knex 3.3's `Client.destroy` destroys the pool only when one is set, then sets it to `undefined`. So it is idempotent and does not throw on an already-destroyed pool. After this change, a caller's `disconnect()` on a refused instance destroys the fresh, empty pool: still a no-throw no-op.

**Inheritance:** `SqliteWasmDriver` and `TursoDriver` (local mode) call `super.connect()`, so they inherit the release. For wasm it is the same `knex.destroy()` the dev resolver's `closeQuietly` already performs on that rejection. Turso's own steps after `super.connect()` never ran on that path. Neither package is edited.

## Pins (`sql-driver-25084-sqlite-refused-connect-release.test.ts`)

Read straight after the rejection, with no `disconnect()` first:

- a damaged file whose header says WAL (byte 18 = 2), under `NODE_ENV=production`: the same `SqliteDatabaseFileError` (`SQLITE_CORRUPT`, the filename, `cause.code` `SQLITE_CORRUPT`, the cause's message inside), the directory holds `archive.db` alone (no `-shm` / `-wal`), and the bytes are unchanged;
- `SQLITE_NOTADB`, `SQLITE_CORRUPT`, `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`: the same refusal, and no descriptor open on the file, counted by the operating system (`/proc/self/fd`, Linux; `describe.runIf`);
- reuse: a second `connect()` on the same refused instance gives the same refusal, and after the file is restored from a good copy, a third `connect()` resolves and the query answers `[{ a: 7 }]`;
- a release that fails (`knex.destroy` rejects once): the refusal is still the `SqliteDatabaseFileError`, and `warn` received the release failure;
- CONTROLS: a healthy file connects, answers, and keeps its handle until `disconnect()`; a healthy WAL file connects, writes and reads, with its `-shm` / `-wal` held open beside it.

The #25019 pin's docblock (`expectLeftAsItWas`) said the refused connection keeps `-shm` / `-wal` until it is closed. That is no longer true, so the comment is updated. Its assertions are unchanged.

## Ablation (fix committed first; `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restore blob == `HEAD` `b4bd77749243`, `git diff HEAD` empty)

- **A: the release call removed** (anchor `if (this.isSqlite) await this.releaseRefusedSqliteConnection();`, 1 → 0): 5 red / 3 green. RED: the WAL sibling pin, NOTADB fd, CORRUPT fd, reuse, release-failure. GREEN: both CONTROLS, and the CANTOPEN pin. That pin is green either way, because a CANTOPEN open never held a handle (see the table). It stays as the "same refusal" pin.
- **B: only `this.knex.initialize()` removed** (1 → 0): 1 red / 7 green. The reuse pin fails with `connect() resolved for a file the datasource cannot use`, which is the hazard described above.

The test imports `./sql-driver.js` from source, so neither leg needs a `dist/` rebuild.

## Verification (head `808e62f0d`, merged with `origin/main` `03966ceae`: already up to date)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql typecheck`: exit 0. `tsc --listFiles` includes both edited test files.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql test`: exit 0. 228 files passed and 12 skipped; 3720 tests passed and 210 skipped. The skips are the live pg / mysql cells; that package's reporter names them.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-datasource test`: exit 0. 53/53 files, 930/930 tests. It was run after building its closure, and the rebuilt `driver-sql` `dist` carries `releaseRefusedSqliteConnection` (2 hits).
- The four SQLite file-refusal pin files (#23696, #24960, #25019, #25084): 26/26.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 70 lines, run one by one, each exit code captured before any pipe. 68 exited 0 on the first run. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, no `dist/`) and `check:type-check-debt` hit the runner's 300 s cap. Both exited 0 when re-run after the full build. `--ran` reconciliation: "70 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 70 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)". Full build (`pnpm exec turbo run build --concurrency=2`): exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core test:repo`: exit 0, 6/6 files, 82/82 tests.

## Acceptance notes

- `SqlDriver.disconnect()` followed by `connect()` on the same instance resolves without a working pool. That is the same code-less "Unable to acquire a connection" this PR avoids on the refusal path. It predates this PR. Whether any caller connects an instance again after `disconnect()` was NOT MEASURED, and it is left as is.
